solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Settled camp enclosing one's settlement

indicators.note: the two outer pieces wrap round the possessive, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: settled, as in sat down, gives SAT
a camp is a faction or side within a group
one's read as 'one is', I (one) plus S

explanation.surface: A fixed camp holds the land one has settled on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosing' acts on the two outer pieces together; 'Settled' and 'settlement' look like a pair, but only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement of a debt or claim is its satisfaction, the meeting of what is owed.

clue.text: Vegetable stew once prepared preserving recipe

indicators.note: preserving means holding something safe inside, so one piece goes within the other
food that is prepared is made ready, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A cook makes a stew from an old recipe kept in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges STEWONCE into SWEETCON, and 'preserving' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is maize grown for eating, a common vegetable side dish.

clue.text: Name of boxer and some rottweilers!

definitions.text: Name of boxer and some rottweilers!

parts.words: Name of boxer and some rottweilers!
parts.note: the surname of the famous heavyweight Mike, also a tough name owners like to give big dogs

explanation.surface: A name shared by a heavyweight fighter and plenty of guard dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' could be the dog breed, matching the rottweilers; it is Mike, the American heavyweight champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike of that surname was world heavyweight champion, and the name is popular for muscular dogs.

clue.text: Winds round reel

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for winds is read backwards

parts.note: winds, as a verb, loops: coils round

explanation.surface: A line winds round a fishing reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a cylinder on which thread or film is wound, much like a reel.

clue.text: Doctor instead to produce cures

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instead of a doctor, something else is used to make remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject; it is the verb telling you to rearrange INSTEAD and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidotes are remedies that counteract poisons, so they are cures.

clue.text: Put differently, Tory leader charged with reprimand

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: charged, as in rushed, gives RAN
to slate is to criticise or reprimand harshly

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief is charged and told off, in other words.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to render words in another language, expressing them differently.

clue.text: Willow is more blooming having top removed

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: rosier means pinker and healthier, more blooming

explanation.surface: A willow looks healthier after being pruned at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having top removed' drops the R from ROSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose pliant shoots are used for basketwork.

clue.text: Impossible if blues fan changes, accepting Queen

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the queen goes inside the rearranged letters
the fan changes, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A football fan who switches from the Blues to support the royals would be unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blues' suggests a football club's fans; 'changes' rearranges the letters to INSUFFABLE and 'accepting' takes the Queen in.
explanation.definitionFit: Insufferable means unbearable, as an impossible person is to put up with.

clue.text: Scotsman's tatty accompaniment?

parts.note: in Scotland tatties are potatoes, and the turnip mash served alongside them with haggis has a Scots name

explanation.surface: A scruffy Scot needs a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tatty' looks like shabby, but in Scots tatties are potatoes, traditionally eaten with mashed turnip and haggis on Burns Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps is the Scots word for turnips or swedes, eaten with tatties.

clue.text: Isolation's over with good man facing apartheid

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ST, saint, is a good man
apartheid was a system of racial segregation, an example of racism

explanation.surface: A country is shut out once a saintly figure stands against apartheid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' joins the pieces. The surface recalls South Africa's sporting boycott over apartheid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism is exclusion from a group, leaving someone in isolation.

clue.text: Spin Premier's spouting on broadcast

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, below the first piece
a spouting premier is talking wildly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds an S, read as PREMIERS
broadcast means sent out, transmitted

explanation.surface: A prime minister's spin doctor tells half-truths on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spouting' makes MISREPRE; 'on' puts the broadcast piece below it in this down clue. 'Spin' is the spin doctor's art, not rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin a story is to put a misleading slant on it, to give a false account.

clue.text: A French aroma preceded getting separated

parts.note: un is French for a
a tang is a sharp smell or taste
led means went in front, preceded

explanation.surface: A French scent came first and then got loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Untangled strands are freed from one another, so they have been separated.

clue.text: Starts to stand up, riding foaming sea

definitions.text: Starts to stand up, riding foaming sea

indicators.note: starts are first letters, so the opening of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A surfer stands up and rides the foaming waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and supplies the letters, an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: To surf is to stand up on a board riding the breaking waves of the sea.

clue.text: Filled initially working trowel around palmetto ends?

definitions.text: Filled initially working trowel around palmetto ends?

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the next word
around tells us the rearranged letters go round the next piece
trowel is worked over, so its letters are rearranged
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gardener fills a pot with a trowel, putting in a palm plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' makes LOWERT; 'around' wraps it round the palmetto's ends just before its final letter. A palmetto is a small palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmetto, a small palm, would be planted in a pot of soil filled by trowel.

clue.text: Select former unit on hospital department

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former
a cell is a basic unit, of life or organisation
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Picking a former team member for a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces, ENT following in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Select, as an adjective, means choice and of top quality, which is excellent.

clue.text: Brig stripped vessel taken by fellow warship

indicators.note: taken by means held inside, so the pieces go into the fellow

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, only the middle of the word remains

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquid

explanation.surface: A two-masted brig is stripped and captured by another fighting ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brig' looks like the ship type; 'stripped' removes its outer letters, and 'taken by' puts the result and the vessel inside the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned armed ship licensed to attack enemy shipping, a warship of sorts.

clue.text: She's caught in a made-up story

definitions.text: She's caught in a made-up story

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the word for a fiction

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A woman finds herself trapped inside a piece of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-in-one: Lewis Carroll's heroine is caught up in Wonderland, a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's girl who falls into Wonderland lives inside an invented tale.

clue.text: Footprint 'Rover' trailed catching lone wolf

indicators.note: catching means holding within, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A dog's footprint leads trackers to a solitary wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert keeps to themself, a loner like a lone wolf.

clue.text: Outing in charge of old characters

parts.note: a run is an outing or trip

explanation.surface: A trip in charge of some elderly eccentrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people; it means letters of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic letters were the characters of the old Germanic alphabets, such as the futhark.

clue.text: He studies bug, otherwise holding wasp's tail

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the final letter goes inside

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: a tail is the last letter

parts.note: or means otherwise, as an alternative

explanation.surface: An entomologist examines a bug, or else holds a wasp by the sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests insect, which is right, but also hints at a phone tap for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector examines and scrutinises things, so he is one who studies.

clue.text: Chick left creating pandemonium

parts.note: chick and babe are both slang for an attractive young woman

explanation.surface: A girl walking out caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' is the link. The Tower of Babel brought the confusion of tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: Babel stands for a noisy confusion of voices, from the biblical tower.

clue.text: Front of bib with dribble from drink

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ooze is to dribble or seep slowly

explanation.surface: A baby's bib gets dribble from a drink down its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Cursed bird when draped round neck?

definitions.text: Cursed bird when draped round neck?

parts.words: Cursed bird when draped round neck?
parts.note: in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner a sailor shoots a seabird and its corpse is hung about his neck as a curse

explanation.surface: An unlucky bird worn like a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a burden of guilt, from the Ancient Mariner poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The great seabird hung around the Mariner's neck became the idiom for a persistent burden.

clue.text: Soak hit on hot European

parts.note: to bat is to hit
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Wash after striking a hot European.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to soak in water.

clue.text: Last item removed in strip?

parts.note: in a striptease the final garment off is a skimpy piece of underwear

explanation.surface: The final thing taken off in a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' could be a comic strip or a sports kit; it is a striptease.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is minimal underwear, the final garment shed in a strip.

clue.text: Run following sweetheart, tense holding hands

definitions.text: Run following sweetheart, tense holding hands

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the run comes after the sweetheart

parts.note: the heart, the middle letter, of sweet is E
to lope is to run with long strides
hands are workers, men
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous couple run off hand in hand to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-in-one: the whole clue pictures the act. 'holding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is running away secretly with a lover to marry.

clue.text: Being performed by Lyric Theatre?

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: A show staged at the Lyric Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lyric Theatre' looks like the London venue; 'Lyric' is the poem and 'Theatre' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a chain name for cinemas, and the word comes from a Greek theatre for music.

clue.text: Boxer wet leg and I threw wobbly!

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A fighter with a damp leg throws a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'threw wobbly' reads as a tantrum, but 'threw' is fodder and 'wobbly' alone signals rearranging WETLEGITHREW; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A welterweight is a boxer in the weight class between lightweight and middleweight.
